source_review.notes: Checked all fifteen primary references. Kubernetes SIG Multicluster MCS types, Kubernetes multi-zone/topology/Service/EndpointSlice/production guidance, Cluster API, Google Cloud regional architecture, AWS multi-region recovery/operations guidance, and Google SRE cascading-failure guidance support the bounded current claims.

evidence: Reviewed topology-domain sets, correlation relation, eligibility set, regional demand/capacity, failure set, recovery load, data epoch/authority/commit/lag, client failover time, and regional evidence notation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation keeps physical/logical topology, hard eligibility, aggregate capacity, data authority and observed client recovery distinct.

evidence: Executed the nine-region synthetic eligibility audit and reproduced eligible=3 with one each residency, trust, data, stale-health, capacity and recovery rejection.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The categories total nine and the 91-second health observation correctly exceeds the 30-second freshness boundary.

evidence: Verified eligibility as conjunction of residency, trust, capability, data, dependency, health, failure capacity and recovery; verified the necessary post-failure aggregate-capacity inequality and fenced epoch transition.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The text correctly states that aggregate capacity is necessary but insufficient because per-region constraints and data authority still apply.

evidence: Reviewed zone/region/provider correlation, global identity/DNS/KMS/registry/control loss, partition and stale intent, exporter impersonation, telemetry blindness, DNS caches and long sessions, replica lag, split brain, cold quotas, retry overload, incompatible rollout, compromise, residency and stale-region failback.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans topology, control, traffic, data, capacity, identity, security, observability, provider, tenant, continuity and cost boundaries.

evidence: Traced topology identity, eligibility, regional autonomy, traffic/data, capacity and transition-evidence invariants through placement, discovery, partition, deployment, failover, failback, game day and retirement.
invariant_checking.notes: The invariants prevent label-based identity, soft-score policy override, unsafe global dependency, routing/write-authority confusion, nominal-only headroom and DNS-only completion.

evidence: Verified two three-region deployments with identical normal healthy clusters: independent regional dependencies versus all regions relying on identity/KMS/registry/control in region A.
proof_review.notes: The indistinguishability construction correctly refutes resilience claims based on region count and motivates dependency/outcome evidence.

evidence: The region-count counterexample is explicitly labeled a proof sketch and states construction, consequence and stronger necessary evidence.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No cloud topology, MCS primitive, capacity formula or game-day practice is represented as a universal proof.

evidence: The placement audit is explicitly synthetic and disclaims provider independence and real regional safety; all ten examples are scenarios; current product behavior is retrieval-dated.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No real evacuation, measured RPO/RTO, capacity test, provider independence, tenant result or external review is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed outcomes/failure sets, topology identity, regional cells, common dependencies, hierarchical control, partitions, placement, MCS identity/discovery, endpoint publication, traffic/DNS, data authority/fencing, capacity, rollout, identity/policy, observability, failover, failback, exercises and cost.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementability with immutable topology IDs, authoritative correlation, scoped global intent, local autonomy/expiry, filter-before-score placement, authenticated endpoint leases, routing hysteresis, writer epochs, quota/headroom inventories, state-machine transitions, representative game days and cost attribution.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified required order, one-page review, definitions/formulas, twelve-step mechanism, six invariants, bounded proof sketch, executable audit, eighteen trade-offs, thirty misconceptions, ten examples, ten connections, fifteen references, and five answered exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
